Krzepice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Krzepice, Poland

Not demolished. Krzepice, granted town rights in 1347, saw Jewish settlement begin in the early 17th century; population grew to 49% (1,057) by 1875, still 43% (1,772) by 1921. A 1940 ghetto held about 1,800 Jews before their deportation to Auschwitz-Birkenau in mid-1942. This cemetery, existing by 1740 (its oldest tombstone date) with burials continuing to 1946, is remarkably notable for its collection of 402 cast-iron matzevot - one of the largest concentrations of this rare form in Europe, most produced at the Kuźnica Stara smelter - alongside 310 stone tombstones. Since 1997, successive restoration projects (the Polish Union of Jewish Students, the youth-led 'Antyschematy' project in 2000 and 2009, and a 2014 POLIN Museum-commissioned inventory) have documented and protected the site; a 2013 monument by Romuald Cieśla honors the Lipszyc and Zelcer families, funded by an anonymous descendant.
